question.text: Nilgiri Credit Opportunities Fund (Cat II) wants to appoint external members to its Investment Committee (IC) who were NOT disclosed in the PPM, investor agreement, or other fund documents at onboarding. Under SEBI's IC governance framework for Cat I/II AIFs (with the INR 70 crore investor-waiver carve-out for the responsibility provision), what investor consent is required for such an appointment of undisclosed external IC members?

answer.text: Consent of at least 75% of the external IC members
Consent of at least 75% of investors by value of their commitment to the AIF
Unanimous consent of ALL investors in the AIF
Simple majority of the IC, with no investor consent required

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, IC members are responsible for the investment decisions of the AIF, and an investor whose commitment is INR 70 crore or more may waive the application of that responsibility provision. Where external IC members are NOT disclosed in the PPM, investor agreement or other fund documents at the time of investor onboarding, they may be appointed only with the consent of at least 75% of investors by value of their commitment to the AIF. The Trap: The 75%-of-external-members option is not the source-backed rule for appointment of undisclosed external IC members. The unanimous-of-all option overstates the threshold. The simple-majority-of-IC option ignores the investor-consent requirement entirely. Note: The INR 70 crore figure is a per-investor waiver of the IC-responsibility provision, not a threshold for the appointment-consent rule.
